guide.title: Splinting & Bandaging
guide.lead: Splint the joint above and below a bone injury, or the bones above and below a joint injury, in the position found unless circulation is lost. Pad, secure and check pulse, movement and sensation before and after – every time.

steps.title: Check PMS
steps.text: Pulse, movement and sensation below the injury; remove rings and watches.

steps.title: Choose
steps.text: Rigid, vacuum, sling and swath, traction (mid-shaft femur only), pelvic binder.

steps.title: Position
steps.text: As found. If the limb is pulseless and severely angulated, one gentle in-line traction to restore circulation, per protocol.

steps.title: Secure
steps.text: Joint above and below; pad bony points and gaps; straps not over the injury.

steps.title: Recheck PMS
steps.text: Document before and after; loosen if circulation worsens.

sections.title: Which splint?
rows: Scoop or vacuum mattress, padding between the legs – no traction
Sling and swath, padded armpit, as found
Rigid or vacuum splint including elbow and wrist; hand in position of function
In the position found, bones above and below

sections.title: Traction splint
exclude: Knee or lower leg or ankle injury on the same side
Partial amputation or bone ends out of the wound

sections.title: Dislocations
items: Splint in the position found; don't reduce unless your protocol allows a specific reduction
Pulseless limb: urgent transport; one gentle realignment attempt if protocol allows

quiz.q: Closed mid-shaft forearm fracture: correct technique?
options: Immobilise elbow and wrist, pad, check PMS before and after

quiz.q: Motorcyclist with a short, externally rotated leg and groin pain, thigh not deformed. Traction splint?
options: No: likely hip fracture – scoop or vacuum mattress, pad between the legs

quiz.q: Fall onto the shoulder: arm held away from the body, squared-off shoulder. You:
options: Sling and swath in the position found, pad the armpit, check PMS

quiz.q: Teenager with a deformed mid-thigh after a fall. Before a traction splint you must rule out:
options: Hip, pelvic, knee and lower-leg injuries on the same side

quiz.explanation: Bone injury: the joints above and below.

quiz.q: After splinting, the fingers are cold and numb. You:
options: Loosen and re-pad the splint and recheck

quiz.q: Pulseless, severely angulated lower leg fracture. Per most protocols:
options: One gentle in-line traction to realign, then splint and recheck

flashcards.question: Splinting principles
flashcards.answer: Joint above and below (or bones above and below a joint), position found, pad, secure away from the injury, PMS before and after.

flashcards.question: Traction splint contraindications
flashcards.answer: Hip or pelvic injury, knee or lower-leg injury on the same side, partial amputation or protruding bone. Only for isolated mid-shaft femur fractures.

flashcards.question: Dislocations
flashcards.answer: Splint as found and transport. Reduce only where your protocol allows; a pulseless limb is urgent.

flashcards.question: Sling and swath
flashcards.answer: Sling supports the forearm; swath binds the arm to the chest. For clavicle, shoulder and upper-arm injuries.

flashcards.question: Buddy taping
flashcards.answer: Tape an injured finger or toe to its neighbour with padding between; check circulation before and after.

flashcards.question: Spinal motion restriction equipment
flashcards.answer: Collar, extrication device, long board for extrication only, scoop and vacuum mattress for transport.

flashcards.question: When the spine can be cleared (NEXUS)
flashcards.answer: No midline tenderness, normal alertness, no intoxication, no focal deficit, no distracting injury.

flashcards.question: PMS checks
flashcards.answer: Pulse (radial or pedal), Movement (wiggle fingers or toes), Sensation (light touch). Before and after every splint.

critical.scenario: Cyclist hit by a car: deformed right mid-thigh, no hip or knee pain, no other injuries, stable vital signs.
critical.question: Splint and critical steps?

options.t: Traction splint for an isolated mid-shaft femur fracture; check PMS before and after; analgesia; monitor for blood loss

critical.explanation: A femur can hide 1–1.5 L of blood.
critical.kpi: Applies a traction splint with appropriate checks

critical.scenario: 17-year-old football player with an obviously dislocated shoulder begs you to 'pop it back in'.
critical.question: Management?

options.t: Explain that you'll splint it as found (sling and swath, padded armpit), check PMS, ice and analgesia, and transport

options.f: Risk of nerve and vessel injury.

critical.explanation: Associated fractures need X-ray before reduction.
critical.kpi: Splints a dislocation in the position found

critical.scenario: Fall of about 4 m onto lumber: severe low back pain, weak legs, a head wound.
critical.question: Motion restriction approach?

options.t: Manual stabilisation, collar, log-roll onto a scoop or vacuum mattress, pad, recheck neuro, trauma centre

options.f: New weakness means possible cord injury.

options.t: Long board for the whole transport
options.f: Use a scoop or vacuum mattress.

critical.explanation: Neuro deficit plus midline pain requires spinal motion restriction.
critical.kpi: Applies spinal motion restriction for neurologic deficit
